title: QuantBench: profile-driven load harness for quality/perf regression detection
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a reproducible, profile-driven benchmarking harness (QuantBench) that evaluates quantization configurations (FP16, INT8, INT4) under realistic load to detect regressions in tokens/sec and p95 latency while measuring quality degradation against baseline FP16. This ticket covers harness design, implementation, and initial sweep against two representative models (redwood-small-1 and open-arch-14B). Deliverables: automated CI job, dashboarding hooks, regression alerting rules, and sampling plan for human validation.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can replay 3 production-like load profiles (burst, steady, tail) with configurable concurrency and request distributions
For each quant profile the harness reports tokens/sec, p95 latency, failure rate and a quality vector (embedding-sim, rouge-l, ppl) and stores results in the benchmark bucket
CI job triggers weekly sweep and posts regression PR comments when tokens/sec drops >7% or p95 increases >12% vs baseline FP16
Dashboard visualizes historical tokens/sec and p95 per quant profile and highlights regressions automatically
Noise-tolerant statistical test implemented (paired bootstrap) with configurable alpha and minimum sample size
harness_config: calibration_set: 5k examples sampled from production prompt corpus (stratified by length)
concurrency: default 16 worker threads, adjustable per run
batching_policy: emulate runtime continuous batching with max_batch=64 and latency_slo_ms=200
metrics_collected: tokens_sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, errors_per_1e6, memory_peak_gb, gpu_util, cpu_util
quality_metrics: embedding_cos_sim (using text-embed-ada baseline), rouge-l, perplexity (token-level)
evaluation_methodology: Baseline: FP16 performance profile measured across same harness runs
Quant profiles: symmetric INT8 per-channel, asymmetric INT8 per-tensor, mixed INT4 for attention/kernels, and FP16 smaller-memory configs
Calibration: KL-divergence and MSE on activation distributions with 2k calibration samples per profile

Regression rules: tokens/sec drop >7% OR p95 latency increase >12% triggers candidate regression; quality filter requires embedding_cos_sim >= 0.985 or rouge-l drop <= 1.5 points else mark quality regression
Statistical testing: paired bootstrap on tokens/sec and p95 with 1k resamples, alpha=0.05, report CI and p-value
Human validation: sample 50 generation pairs (baseline vs quant) for each profile when automated quality tests flag borderline failures
rollout_plan: Stage 1: implement harness and run local sweeps on dev infra; attach results to PR
Stage 2: integrate sweep into weekly CI and wire Grafana dashboard panels
Stage 3: add regression bot that opens PR comments with links to failing runs and suggested rollback profiles
Stage 4: coordinate with ops to gate deploys for Dedicated and Private if regression detected on production-weighted profile
risks_mitigation: Synthetic load mismatch: mitigate by sampling production traces and replaying header-level routing to approximate real request mix
Noisy measurements: use warmed runs and 5-run median trimming plus paired bootstrap to reduce false positives
Calibration drift between models: keep profile metadata tied to model version and record seed/calibration artifacts in S3
Human review scale: triage to only require human review when automated tests give mixed signals (quality borderline and perf degradation)
